title: Can AI help find and evaluate fun game ideas?
author: lazy_code_bear
selftext:
I made a ChatGPT skill to make game concept exploration more focused. It helps me:

Explore different kinds of player appeal

Identify the core gameplay loop

Compare ideas for fun potential

Scope a small playable prototype

The video shows a concept I brought to the process and developed into a prototype with AI assistance. Using the skill exposed two problems:

Ideas: AI can recognize a promising idea, but generating one has been harder.

Fun: How can we make AI’s assessment of fun more accurate and systematic, especially when playtesters are hard to find?

How do you approach these parts of AI-assisted game development?

comments.author: BertJohn
comments.body:
Idea's isn't the problem with catching players attention, People play games with literal dice, Cards, Hell even clicking the game was a game that did fantastic. The problem is effort & polish. People don't care if a game mechanic is there if its not polished and fun to play with. 

  
Look at flappy bird, Have AI remake it, And see how theres a serious lack of polish comparatively between the two? That you can't replicate with AI unfortunately.

replies.author: lazy_code_bear
replies.body: Thanks, that’s a helpful point. I’ve been focusing a lot on the mechanic, but I’ll put more effort into the feel and visual polish too. I’ll do it in small steps so I can see what improves the experience before investing too much.
